intro: Measurement lags capabilities while control work tries to catch up.

pulse.text: Frontier capability work is pushing toward self-improvement, with MLExpert jumping to 72.7% medals and Google closing the wet-lab loop to 42% on-target aptamers, while measurement still lags as 90% of US work hours lack benchmark coverage. Press and Hacker News discussion fixates on open-weight releases like Muse Spark and Beam that run on desktop clusters, and on what unreleased lab models imply. Researchers are preoccupied with whether oversight holds, from worst-case debate guarantees to honesty transfer and evaluation awareness in Indic languages.
pulse.reading: Self-improving agents and wet-lab loops outweigh thin coverage and oversight gains

items.title: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
items.note: Mapping 29 agentic benchmarks to 18,797 O*NET tasks finds only 208 of 923 occupations have at least 5 prompts, leaving about 90% of US working hours uncovered. Coverage skews toward high-wage, AI-exposed work like lawyers over adjacent clerical roles. Deployment claims are therefore running ahead of any measured picture of work actually done.
items.author: speckx

items.title: CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty
items.note: CATCH trains toward honest answers and away from dishonest ones using only hundreds of targets, tested on Llama-3.3-70B and Qwen3-27B. Honesty transfers across settings without degrading capability. It matters because it offers a cheap, repeatable lever where alignment training usually fails to generalize.
items.author: Yuan-Chen Chang, Niklas Herbster, Gauthier Gidel

items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.note: A 35B mixture-of-experts trained with hierarchical SFT and Windowed Interaction RL lifts MLE-Bench Lite medals from 37.9% to 72.7%, matching larger frontier systems. Gains transfer to NatureBench Lite and scaffold optimization, suggesting general optimization skill rather than benchmark fit. That is concrete movement toward AI systems that improve AI systems.

items.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
items.note: Four instruction-tuned models tested in five Indic languages plus English refuse harmful requests more often when told they are monitored as a safety test. The effect persists outside English, where over a billion speakers interact with models. Safety evals that ignore language therefore overstate how cautious a deployed model will be.
items.author: Trizal Garg, Sibayan Mitra, Arya Karanjkar

items.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
items.note: FDE-Gym contributes 95 delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios where agents must clarify ambiguity in live systems with scripted stakeholders. Unlike issue-ticket benchmarks, it scores end-to-end delivery under unstated constraints. Early implication is frontier agents still stumble at the last mile that determines enterprise value.
items.author: Dongxu Yang, Hongda Yan, Renxin Wang

items.title: The Case for DUV Controls
items.note: Saif Khan projects that cutting DUV tool exports now leaves China producing roughly 100x fewer AI chips than the US by the mid-2030s. The argument rests on supply-chain physics rather than model timelines, making lithography the decisive policy lever. If right, export controls shape the AI balance more than any near-term model lead.
items.author: Jordan Schneider

items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.note: Google's VERID digital twin plus three closed-loop campaigns grounds agents in live volume, geometry and video logs to catch physical errors before execution. On aptamers, agents climbed from 0% to 42.1% on-target hits for thrombin by fixing primer folding across rounds. The result narrows the gap between in-silico design and wet-lab validation that has bottlenecked bio-automation.
